title: Overcharging & Recording Without My Knowledge!
text:
I wasn't even aware that there were auto-recurring charges to my credit card resulting in hundreds of dollars of loss + credit card interest. I used it 2-3 times, and got charged for 1.5 years. 

Also, the app was recording my activities when it was installed and conferences online, some of them very confidential without my knowledge. I suspect that my data was also sold to online data brokers, which would explain the increase in targeted ads. It's also a security risk. What an invasion of privacy without my knowledge! And it wasn't installed for at least a year, yet I was charged for it nonetheless. It's borderline fraud.

title: Seems good, but must register to import audio file
text:
Hi. I was anticipating a great way to create a transfer from importing a .vtt file, and then extracting a transcript. To get to that point I was able to remove the adds with touching  always small and off to the right or left corner X. 

This X option is well devoted, off of the way, seems to give many people the impression here and in most apps as if you gave to register on that page to use the free app. 

Well. I clicked the x, and started to import my audio file. But I only had two options pre register to a “plan” that will charge you after a set number of days. Or exit. 

Why can’t all apps be above board, as a very few and excellent apps do, allow you to completely use the features first free (remember, free is NOT register-to-be-free, register first is a way to have a high likelihood of keeping a paying customer), but not here. This policy is $$$$ driven. 

I choose the Free for only to find out it doesn’t give you full reign. 

That Free door must have a an honest and transparent intent with a sign: Free-kinda-cause you must be forced into a x number of days without charge, of course you can delete before then….(!)

I’ve spent way too much time in a hopefully level comment. 

I had liked the developer response on low ratings, which read rather honest and “good people”. 

If I have guests over for free food, I don’t ask them to leave a credit card deposit upon entering, should they make my bathroom trashy, right? After all, I’m good, I will return your deposit if the bathroom is clean, when you leave. That is not a good and free existence. I’ll delete and get another.

title: Needs work
text: This is not the transcription app for you if your meetings are heated and people are talking over each other or if anyone mumbles or speaks too fast, or has an accent. In the 56 meetings I recorded and used this app to transcribe, all but one had to be edited, line by line.    However, compared to the other transcription apps I used, at least this one let me edit the speaker names and what they said.

title: So Sad
text: Paywalled out of seeing the last 19 minutes of an enthralling conversation because I didn’t press stop at the 89 minute mark to start a new one. My fault for being engaged in the conversation. It was a very unpleasant feeling seeing the message that Otter has it transcribed but if I don’t pay up to upgrade to Business from my 99.99/year Premium subscription, then I can get lost. Even funnier is how it promises 90 minutes, but I was cut off mid sentence 12 seconds before 89min. I want to be mad but am simply sad. Is this what they call late stage capitalism? Goodbye Otter and good riddance.

title: Wow.  This is how former kings fall
text: Otter was the king of AI transcribing before ChatGPT was a thing.   The secret weapon.  Then like many lazy kings they do things at 50%.  Example: I had a dozen meetings last week so I paid the quite expensive monthly subscription cost. Now I need otter to do what every other AI platform can do today: go through each of those 12 meeting scripts and take notes for each meeting in the following ways:  then I take the time and give the AI about two paragraphs of specific requests.  Easy stuff like for each meeting use the contents to title the meeting in a more helpful way then the otter AI meeting titles. “Chuck” “Bob” should be “met with Bob to discuss sales trends over last two years”.  Ok? And I include mention like use subtitles for “person speaking” and put what they say under their name per each convo.  So what does dodo do? I mean otter.  It just puts “person name” thirty times throughout the notes.  Bro.  Really? ChatGPT 3.5 turbo was great but 2023 is the past homie.   Somebody at otter is pinching Pennies and thinking shortsighted when they should be claiming ground as king of kings using at least sonnet latest.   Not running a home made LLM on a Mac Studio cluster to save money. Because no way bro.  I am definitely finding a better transcription solution from here on out.  For 20 bucks or whatever  paid for this that’s a bad value these days and there’s even a limit to the number of minutes I have.  Fight over crumbs and you’ll be fighting over crumbs for sure in five years when you’re down to the two original founders again running things.   But hey. I’m just one guy.  ✌️

title: Underwhelming for a specialized tool
text:
I’ve been paying for otter for around a year and a half. It’s hard to persuade myself to stay with it given the evolving options in the market.

Transcription inaccuracies are surprisingly high, even after adding custom vocabulary . Sometimes when I go to copy transcript, I realize that a large section of the conversation just wasn’t recorded.

Even when it does record everything, it takes too long to transcribe files, so when I get back from my morning walk where I dictate my action plan for the day, I still have to wait five or more minutes. 

Otter needs to be an obviously superior tool or it will lose out to Claude App, ClickUp Brain Max, or similar tools.

title: Used to be my go to…
text: Calling a paid subscription “pro“ but placing an additional paywall limit at 90 minutes per meeting transcription is an absolute miss. Otter.ai’s 1200-minute monthly limit is fair, but user should be able to access as needed, not limited per recording. As such, after several years of satisfying service, I am now forced me to move on to other providers with more user-centric options. It’s a shame too, because Otter.ai is an excellent service. But I’m not paying triple the price for what is essentially just the ability to have an occasional two hour meeting notated.

title: highly unusual behavior in the Otter mobile app.
text:
I am writing to report highly unusual behavior in the Otter mobile app.The app has suddenly started misspelling words frequently. This is completely uncharacteristic of the software, which normally provides perfect spelling and self-corrects seamlessly. Furthermore, the app is now enforcing strict usage limits on my account, even though I used it just a few days ago with zero restrictions.Because of these concurrent issues—frequent typos that never used to happen and sudden usage blocks—I am concerned that the app is either malfunctioning or my account has been compromised.Please look into this technical glitch as soon as possible.

Thank you, 

Wendy Alvarado

title: "Award-winning" joke of an app. Save your money.
text:
Don't let the marketing fool you, this app is a massive waste of money. They boast about being an "award-winning" platform, but they can't even handle basic processing. I am paying $30 a month, and yet I'm consistently waiting 10, sometimes up to 24 hours, just to get a simple meeting summary and transcript.

If I wanted to wait an entire day to know what happened in my meeting, I would have taken manual notes. The entire selling point of AI meeting assistants is speed and efficiency, both of which are completely non-existent here. Paying premium price for snail-pace delivery is a joke. Avoid this app at all costs.

title: OK. Integrates well with AI.
text: Not that great at identifying names of speakers. My hope is that it would identify a voice and give it a speaker number, but you have to go in and label every speaker even when it’s the same person and you’ve already given them a label. Also, I have not figured out a way to crop transcripts so if you record longer than you meant to, you can’t crop that part out.
